claims.claim: CPU-Z validator data show 32 GB at 37.2 percent of submissions, down 2.5 percent year over year, while 16 GB rose 12.9 percent to 33.0 percent, and Doc TB called it the first year-over-year decline in RAM capacity in that dataset.
claims.episode_span: Configurations of 32 GB are still the most common, at 37.2 percent, down 2.5 percent from a year ago
claims.source_title: CPU-Z Data Shows 16 GB RAM Gaining Ground While 32 GB and 64 GB RAM Shares Shrink
claims.supporting_quote: 32 GB is still the most popular configuration at 37.2% of validations, though its share is down 2.5% compared to a year ago.
